F001.acceptance: upgrade-releases.schema.json + Pydantic model validate a manifest carrying baseline_release + baseline_date and releases[] whose actions carry kind, severity, ordered commands[] with preview|apply|verify|run labels, applies_when, status_probe, success_message, failure_message, human_next_step, docs_url, introduced_commands, and release-level show_on_first_run; load_release_manifest rejects each malformed case (unknown kind/severity/command-label, missing required field, non-date date, unknown key, missing baseline) with a typed error; empty commands[]/null status_probe/null applies_when accepted for advisory actions. Tests cover all cases. A kind=required action with null/empty status_probe is rejected by the loader (required-action invariant, D021); advisory actions may omit it (test covers both). A kind=required action with empty commands[] or no apply-labeled command is rejected (D029); duplicate release ids (manifest-wide) and duplicate action ids within a release are rejected (D030). Tests cover each rejection. A kind=required action missing apply or verify, or with out-of-order labels, is rejected (D036, test). load_release_manifest resolves releases.json as a package-relative resource that loads outside the repo root and off-git (D045, test). A required action with a blank/whitespace-only command string is rejected (D047, test). Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048).

F002.acceptance: docs/upgrade/releases.json validates under upgrade-releases.schema.json, carries a baseline, and contains the Experience Readiness advisory entry/entries (empty commands/null status_probe, severity optional) plus the canonical-discovery required entry with ordered commands (preview+apply+verify), non-null status_probe, applies_when, success/failure copy, and introduced_commands. A test asserts the seed loads, the baseline is present, and the canonical-discovery action is kind required with a non-null status_probe and a verify-labeled command. The baseline orders strictly below the earliest seeded release so every seeded release is in-scope, not exempt history (D039). Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048). releases.json is included as package data in the wheel and sdist and loads from the installed/packaged location (not only the repo tree) (D049, test).

F003.acceptance: predicate_registry resolves status_probe and applies_when keys; canonical_discovery_registered_active returns satisfied=true whenever DontPanic reconciles to registered_active INCLUDING when a stale/malformed evidence file is present (dedicated test) and false (with detail) for stale/missing/unresolved/error; evidence validity gates only canonical_backfill_evidence_valid, not the outcome probe. has_tracked_projects reflects registry presence; status_probe error -> not satisfied (fail-closed) while applies_when error -> applies true. Tests cover every state. An unknown status_probe key resolves to satisfied=false with an error detail (never satisfied), and an unknown applies_when key to applies=true with an error detail; neither crashes assembly (dedicated tests). Every predicate is read-only: a dedicated test runs each predicate and asserts NO registry/evidence/config/ledger/state mutation occurs (no-mutation contract, D028); canonical_discovery_registered_active uses only the reconcile read path. Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048).

F004.acceptance: read_upgrade_state on an absent marker returns an in-memory effective marker and creates NO file (dedicated test asserts upgrade-state.json still absent after read). releases_since is pure and order-correct; first_run_advisories honors show_on_first_run; required actions are independent of the marker. advance_marker/dismiss_advisory are pure and cannot satisfy a required action (test proves a probe-failing required action stays pending after advance_marker). Marker values round-trip through a tmp HOME and contain no secret shapes. A marker whose last_seen_release is absent-from-manifest or predates the earliest release yields all releases as new (required actions still probe-driven), with no exception raised; advisory visibility follows marker_state - predates => ALL advisories, absent => show_on_first_run only (D040/D044) - the two are never conflated (test). read_upgrade_state returns marker_state (absent|predates|known): an ABSENT marker shows only show_on_first_run advisories with null/'never acknowledged' display (never implies acknowledged-latest, D042); an EXISTING predating marker shows ALL manifest advisories (show_on_first_run filter NOT applied, D040); an in-manifest marker shows releases_since(last_seen). Dedicated tests for all three. Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048).

F005.acceptance: assemble_upgrade_report returns {summary:{installed_commit, latest_release_id, last_seen_release, update_state, pending_required, pending_advisory, upstream:{fetched_upstream_commit, upstream_status, remediation}}, required[], advisory[], migration_status[]}; required reflects live status_probe results gated by applies_when and carries ordered commands + success/failure copy; update_state is up_to_date|required_pending|advisories_pending|unknown per the count matrix; upstream_status is computed WITHOUT a network fetch in the default path (test asserts no fetch); installed_commit + upstream degrade to 'unknown' off-git. Tests cover summary + upstream computation and the pending logic. The summary carries last_seen_commit distinct from installed_commit (D023); each required[] item carries introduced_commands (D022); migration_status[] items expose release id, action id, applies status, probe key, satisfied flag, detail, and an evidence pointer (D024); an unknown predicate key surfaces an error detail with the required action pending and never crashes assembly (D026). introduced_commands is carried on both required[] AND advisory[] report items (D033), not required-only (test). Every required[] and advisory[] item carries the pinned shape: stable item id (upgrade:<release>:<action>), release id, action id, kind, severity, title, detail, applies, ordered commands, success/failure copy, human_next_step, docs_url, introduced_commands, and satisfied+probe-detail when probed (D041, test asserts the shape for both lists). When marker_state=absent the summary shows last_seen_release/last_seen_commit as 'never acknowledged' (null), not latest (D042, test). Each required[]/advisory[] item carries the original applies_when and status_probe keys (not only the resolved applies/satisfied booleans) so JSON output stays auditable (D046, test). Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048). migration_status[] includes every probe-backed action with its state (pending, satisfied, or not-applicable), not only pending, so a satisfied/not-applicable item still appears (D051, test).

F006.acceptance: Doctor's upgrade report mode emits the F005 report (summary incl upstream + required/advisory/migration_status) in both human and JSON form; plain doctor emits exactly one WARN with the remediation command + counts when pending and writes no marker; the check-upstream opt-in is the only path that may perform a network fetch. Tests cover the three render modes, the no-implicit-fetch default, and the read-only render (no marker write) invariant. Each required action's introduced_commands (new command surfaces) appear in both the human report and the JSON output (test). introduced_commands renders for advisory items too (not only required), in human and JSON (test, D033). Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048). An end-to-end test asserts plain doctor and the upgrade report perform ZERO writes (no backfill/migration/config/registry/evidence/ledger/marker), covering the whole path not just probe/marker sub-checks (D050).

F007.acceptance: Doctor's acknowledge flag advances and commits the marker and silences currently-shown advisories, but a required action whose status_probe fails is STILL listed as pending afterward (dedicated test); acknowledge is the only doctor path that writes the marker. Tests cover marker advance + commit, advisory silencing, and the acknowledge-does-not-clear-required invariant. Acknowledge composes with the upgrade report mode in human and JSON form; the post-acknowledge report reflects the advanced marker (advisories silenced, last_seen_release/last_seen_commit updated) while a probe-failing required action still shows pending (dedicated tests, D027). Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048).

F008.acceptance: The dashboard exposes an always-shown upgrade-status signal (status line + update_state + counts + last_seen_release + installed_commit) as a Tools & Setup / Health row present in the up-to-date case too; upgrade_action_items are the drill-down (probe-pending required -> needs_action with its command, undismissed advisory -> advisory, dismissed/satisfied absent/info) with stable ids and a stable-key sort. Tests assert the status row across states and that projections contain no secret shapes. The status projection carries upstream_status and the row reflects behind-newest when known; it never shows 'up to date' while upstream_status is behind (D031, test). The projection carries last_seen_commit and the last-acknowledged display renders it (never installed_commit, which is shown separately as the current checkout) (D037, test). With marker_state=absent the row renders 'never acknowledged' (not a synthetic latest acknowledgement) (D042, test). Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048). The ActionItem source vocabulary (+ sort/validation) admits source='upgrade': an upgrade item validates, is not dropped, and sorts with a stable key in the existing provider path (D052, test).

F009.acceptance: docs/upgrade/README.md documents the manifest + full action field set + baseline scope + first-run policy + no-mutation boundary; CHANGELOG.md links to releases.json and gains an entry for the upgrade-readiness surface; RELEASE_IMPACT.md notes the new surface. If the drift lint is added it is warn-only, baseline-scoped, and does not block. Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048).

F010.acceptance: update_journey_e2e reproduces fresh-update -> doctor WARN -> full report (summary + pending required) -> probe satisfied -> action clears + WARN gone + update_state transition, through the real doctor CLI; a captured live upgrade report (JSON) on the real instance (canonical-discovery item reflecting the actual probe) and the journey transcript are saved under evidence/. The required action is satisfied by running its APPLY-labeled command (the real migration step) and then PROVEN by the verify-labeled command; a broken apply or verify command fails the journey (D032, supersedes D025). The apply-labeled command runs only against a disposable isolated fixture instance (an isolated temp HOME + fixture registry), never the operator's real registry, and is torn down after; the real-instance evidence is the read-only upgrade report only (D043, test/isolation asserted). Test output for this feature is captured under evidence/ at close (D048).
